newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Memtec won't fight Pall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Memtec won't fight Pall.

text.p: Memtec Ltd chairman Denis Hanley said he believed the water filtration company would succeed in its US$280 million takeover bid for Gelman Sciences Inc but was not prepared to be involved in a share market brawl with the much larger Pall Corp.

The board of Michigan-based Gelman would not be receiving a higher bid from Memtec, Hanley told Reuters, even though the target company surprised investors last week by saying it had begun talks with Pall, throwing the merger into doubt.
"We are not interested in a bidding war," he said.
Gelman directors and their shareholders should be attracted to the merger because of the Australian company's profit and sales growth, he said.
Memtec was not about to begin changing the terms of the agreed share swap offer as it had prepared a prospectus, and was about to file registration statements in Washington.

"We are a long way down the track. Pall hasn't at this point in time commenced due diligence or negotiations so they wil have to hurry because we go on a roadshow to sell the transaction this week," Hanley said. If Gelman received a better offer, however, its board had a responsibilty to consider it, he added.

"There is no bid from anybody else and the bottom line is we have prepared a prospectus at a conversion ratio of 1.5 Memtec shares to each Gelman share and there is no intention to change that," said the founder of the acquisitive high tech company.

"The issue for Gelman's board is to determine what is in the best interests of shareholders not only in the current circumstance but over time. Memtec has had a higher growth rate both in terms of sales and eps (earnings per share) and I believe will continue to do so."
Memtec's growth strategy would not be greatly affected if the Gelman deal fell through.
"We will grow 50 percent this year without Gelman and as I say it is a question for Gelman where they might like to hitch their carriage."
Gelman said in late July it had agreed to be acquired by NASDAQ-listed Memtec with a stock swap which valued each Gelman share at about S$35, with the deal set for completion by the end of the year.

Analysts welcomed the deal, saying the rich conversion rate should block out other rivals although Pall Corp and two other U.S. filtration companies were believed to have made merger offers around the middle of the year.
Hanley is not surprised to see Pall on the horizon again.

"This (the Gelman transaction) began as a request for bids and Pall Corp was an original bidder, at least we think they were. The Gelman board determined Memtec was a better proposition and I think it (the current talks) is just simply Pall Corp keeping their hat in the ring.".
Describing the talks as exploratory, Pall Corp said earlier this month that it was in merger talks with Gelman, in line with the latter's rights under the Memtec agreement.
An offer would only be made if it enhanced shareholder value, Pall Corp said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
